reason: E2 shows that thermal exposure at 800 °C forms a protective Cr₂O₃ and spinel oxide layer on a similar equiatomic HEA coating, and states that such layers enhance wear resistance, supporting the first two premises. However, the cited evidence describes a microwave-cladded coating on SS-304, not a sputter-deposited thin film, and does not demonstrate a deliberate pre-oxidation treatment or quantify wear reduction, leaving the third and fourth premises unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Thermal exposure of FeNiCrCoCu (or similar equiatomic HEA) in air at 800 °C forms a protective Cr₂O₃ and spinel oxide layer
The oxide layer enhances wear resistance
A pre-oxidation treatment can deliberately form a coherent, adherent oxide layer on a thin-film coating
The oxide layer acts as a hard, lubricious diffusion barrier that reduces direct metal contact and wear at high temperature
